title: ITIL and AI
group: Value streams, AI and other frameworks (10%)

header.html: Define AI, AI maturity, generative AI and agentic AI; understand how AI assists product and service development, automates processes and is used across the value chain activities; define AI governance; understand the ITIL AI Capability Model
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), category 6

html:
1Key AI terms

Term Meaning
Artificial intelligence (AI) Systems that perform tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, understanding language
AI maturity How capable and well governed an organization is in using AI, from first experiments to everyday use
Generative AI (GenAI) AI that creates new content (text, images, code) from prompts
Agentic AI AI that acts toward a goal on its own: it plans, decides and takes actions, often using tools, with limited human steps
AI governance The direction and control of how AI is selected, used and monitored so it is responsible, safe and aligned with the organization's goals and rules
Exam tip

. GenAI creates content. Agentic AI takes actions. AI governance is governance applied to AI.

ITIL is not a technical AI framework; it provides structure, collaboration, governance and continual improvement for using AI. [Verify live]

2How AI helps

Where Examples
Product and service development Drafting requirements, generating test cases, suggesting designs, reviewing code
Automating processes Routing and classifying tickets, drafting replies, self-service answers
Across the value chain activities Discover: analyze feedback; design: prototypes; build: code help and tests; operate: spot anomalies; support: suggest fixes and answers

AI is guided by the guiding principles: for example, focus on value (use AI where it supports real outcomes), start where you are (reuse existing data and models), and optimize and automate (improve first, then automate). [Verify live]

3The ITIL AI Capability Model

The ITIL AI Capability Model groups AI into six capabilities so organizations can see which risks and opportunities each one brings and govern accordingly:

Capability Plain meaning
Creation Generating new content or solutions
Curation Selecting and organizing information and outputs
Clarification Making things clear: interpreting requests, explaining
Cognition Analysis and reasoning: patterns, predictions, decisions
Communication Natural interaction: chat, voice, virtual assistants
Coordination Orchestrating actions across systems, often autonomously

Exam tip

. The six capabilities all start with C. Remember creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. The wording may vary between sources. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Only one mark is about AI, so learn the six capability names and the difference between generative (creates content) and agentic (acts toward a goal).

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A tool writes a first draft of a project plan from a short prompt. Which term fits?

  • AAgentic AI only
  • BGenerative AI
  • CA service level agreement
  • DA known error
Show the answer

Answer: B. It creates new content from a prompt.

S2An AI assistant plans several steps, calls tools, and updates tickets on its own to reach a goal. Which term fits best?

  • AAgentic AI
  • BA static report
  • CContinuous integration
  • DA basic service relationship
Show the answer

Answer: A. Acting toward a goal on its own is agentic AI.

S3Which statements are CORRECT? (1) AI governance directs and controls how AI is used. (2) ITIL is mainly a technical AI framework. (3) GenAI creates new content. (4) AI cannot support any lifecycle activity.

  • A2 and 4
  • B1 and 3
  • C1 and 4
  • D2 and 3
Show the answer

Answer: B. AI governance directs AI use, and GenAI creates content.

S4Identify the missing word(s). [ ? ] describes how capable and well governed an organization is in using AI.

  • AValue stream
  • BA prototype
  • CA critical success factor
  • DAI maturity
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is AI maturity.

S5Which capability in the ITIL AI Capability Model covers orchestrating actions across systems?

  • ACuration
  • BClarification
  • CCommunication
  • DCoordination
Show the answer

Answer: D. Coordination orchestrates actions.

S6How many capabilities does the ITIL AI Capability Model describe?

  • ASix
  • BFour
  • CFive
  • DEight
Show the answer

Answer: A. It describes six capabilities.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Define generative AI.

Show the answer

AI that creates new content from prompts.

R2What is agentic AI?

Show the answer

AI that plans, decides and acts toward a goal with limited human steps.

R3Define AI governance.

Show the answer

The direction and control of how AI is selected, used and monitored.

R4Name the six AI capabilities.

Show the answer

Creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination.

R5Name one way AI can support the operate activity.

Show the answer

Spotting anomalies.

R6What is AI maturity?

Show the answer

How capable and well governed the organization is in using AI.

Topic Key fact

Value chain AI can help every lifecycle activity
